# The WebMCP surface

<!-- GENERATED by `npm run docs:tools` (tools/gen-tool-docs.ts) from src/webmcp/tools.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Release Airlock registers **27 tools** on `document.modelContext`: 6 reads that answer live, a notebook the agent writes its own conclusions into, 19 proposal tools, and a plan tool. Every string below is read from the tool descriptors themselves, through the same `createAirlockTools` path the page uses — this file is a function of the source, regenerated by `npm run docs:tools`, and the generator fails if the observed surface disagrees with the grant table (`MODE_WRITE_TOOLS`).

## How to read it

- **The surface is a function of console state.** Reads, the notebook and the plan tool are registered once and never leave. Proposal tools are registered per response stage — **triage** (13 tools) → **diagnosis** (17 tools) → **recovery** (27 tools) — each with its own `AbortController`, so moving the stage unregisters and registers tools underneath a live agent session and a real host fires `toolchange`. A tool that leaves is tombstoned and `explain_surface` says why.
- **A write tool cannot execute anything.** Its only successful return is `{ status: "proposed", proposalSeq, note }`: an approval card in front of the operator, and the world unchanged. The engine re-checks the stage, the tier and the dual key **at decision time**, not at proposal time. A client that ignores the surface and calls a write outside its stage gets `{ status: "blocked", blockedSeq, reason }` and an `action.blocked` row in the audit log.
- **Reads are never gated** — the airlock gates consequence, not observability. Every read answers with `asOfSeq` (the log position it reflects); paginated reads are newest-first via `cursor` and pages stay under 1.2KB.
- **Tier** is the risk ladder, 1 (lowest) to 4; the word after it is the domain the lever is attached to. Tier 4 needs the operator to hold the dual key while the write executes. **maps to** is the simulator action key the proposal becomes; the approval card also carries that lever's stated cost from the vocabulary.
- **Annotations** are the WebMCP hints as registered. `untrustedContentHint` marks the one read whose payload can carry external text; the page audits every read into its own event log, so a proposal whose target only ever appeared inside that untrusted text is detected and promoted to the dual key.
- In the **input** column `*` marks a required field. Parameter descriptions, verbatim, are in the appendix.

## Notebook

Present in every stage. Changes nothing in the world and needs no approval — the airlock gates actions, not speech. Returns `{ status: "recorded" }`. `advisesAgainst` is what lets the agent object before the operator's click: reach for that control and its reasoning appears beside it.

| tool | description | input | annotations | stages | maps to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_finding` | Write your current read of the incident into the console so the operator can see it: what you believe is happening and why. Use ruledOut for what you considered and rejected, and advisesAgainst to name an action that would be harmful — if the operator reaches for it, they see your reasoning first. Changes nothing, blocks nobody, needs no approval. | `{ summary*: string, ruledOut: string, advisesAgainst: string }` | readOnlyHint: false | triage · diagnosis · recovery | — |

## Plan

Present wherever writes are. A plan is a claim on the record, never a grant: the tool records the ordered intent and its reason, proposes **step 1 only**, and step N+1 is not proposed until step N has executed. Every step is shape-checked against its proposal tool and the current stage before anything is recorded. Returns `{ status: "planned", planId, steps, note }`.

| tool | description | input | annotations | stages | maps to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `propose_plan` | Propose an ORDERED sequence of 2-8 actions when the order itself matters — when doing the same steps in a different order would cost more. Give the reason the order is load-bearing; the operator reads it before approving anything. Each step is still approved separately, and step N+1 is not proposed until step N has run, so nothing executes ahead of the human. | `{ reason*: string, steps*: { tool*: string, input*: object, because: string }[] }` | readOnlyHint: false | triage · diagnosis · recovery | — |

## Appendix — parameter descriptions, verbatim

### `airlock_status`

- _no input_

### `list_deploys`

- `cursor` (number, optional) — Pass the previous response’s nextCursor for the next (older) page. Omit it for the newest page; there is no page 0.

### `read_logs`

- `cursor` (number, optional) — Pass the previous response’s nextCursor for the next (older) page. Omit it for the newest page; there is no page 0.

### `list_changes`

- _no input_

### `traffic_history`

- `cursor` (number, optional) — Pass the previous response’s nextCursor for the next (older) page. Omit it for the newest page; there is no page 0.

### `explain_surface`

- _no input_

### `record_finding`

- `summary` (string, required) — What you believe is happening, and the evidence for it.
- `ruledOut` (string, optional) — An action you considered and rejected, and why.
- `advisesAgainst` (string, optional) — An action you believe would be harmful, as tool:target (e.g. deploy.rollback:d-201). If the operator reaches for it they see your reasoning first.

### `propose_acknowledge`

- `by` (string, required) — Who is taking it

### `propose_severity`

- `level` (string, required) — sev1, sev2 or sev3

### `propose_escalate`

- `team` (string, required) — Team to page, such as database on-call

### `propose_silence_alerts`

- `silenced` (boolean, required) — true to silence, false to restore

### `propose_status_update`

- `state` (string, required) — investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved
- `text` (string, required) — What customers are told. Plain, specific, no internal jargon.

### `propose_flag_change`

- `id` (string, required) — Flag id, e.g. from list_changes
- `state` (string, required) — Desired state: 'on' or 'off'

### `propose_rollback`

- `deployId` (string, required) — Deploy id to roll back, e.g. from list_deploys

### `propose_rollforward`

- `service` (string, required) — Service id, e.g. from airlock_status

### `propose_env_change`

- `key` (string, required) — Env var key
- `value` (string, required) — New value (redacted in all logs and reads)

### `propose_route_change`

- `id` (string, required) — Route id, e.g. from list_changes
- `target` (string, required) — New target service id

### `propose_deploy_freeze`

- `frozen` (boolean, required) — true to freeze, false to lift

### `propose_canary`

- `deployId` (string, required) — Deploy id from list_deploys
- `percent` (number, required) — Share of traffic, 0-100

### `propose_traffic_change`

- `route` (string, required) — Route id from list_changes
- `percent` (number, required) — Share to send to target, 0-100
- `target` (string, optional) — Where that share should go

### `propose_drain`

- `route` (string, required) — Route id from list_changes

### `propose_rate_limit`

- `route` (string, required) — Route id from list_changes
- `rps` (number, required) — Requests per second to allow

### `propose_restart`

- `service` (string, required) — Service id from airlock_status

### `propose_scale`

- `service` (string, required) — Service id from airlock_status
- `replicas` (number, required) — Desired replica count

### `propose_cache_flush`

- `scope` (string, required) — Which cache, such as session

### `propose_failover`

- `service` (string, required) — Database service id

### `propose_plan`

- `reason` (string, required) — Why THIS order. What goes wrong if the steps are taken the other way round?
- `steps` (array, required) — The actions in the order they must happen. 2 to 8 of them.
- `steps[].tool` (string, required) — The propose_* tool for this step, e.g. propose_rate_limit
- `steps[].input` (object, required) — That tool’s own input object
- `steps[].because` (string, optional) — What this step buys, in one line
